subject: arabic
summary: Arabic script renders correctly joined and right-to-left in the question area, in a large clear face, and the attached reading passage is a sharp page limited to the right text. The serious faults are in grammar cards, where the thing being tested has been lost: vowel marks are stripped from multiple-choice options so the choices look identical, the underlining a question refers to is not shown, and one parsing scheme is cut at the wrong places ('the five nouns' split over two separately-marked rows). Scheme answers are set left-aligned in small grey-black text, much smaller than the question, with a repeated English boilerplate sentence under them that adds nothing. The bottom 'Not claimed yet' strip mixes English and Arabic in one line and scrambles the order. Layout itself holds on both phone and desktop.

issues.title: Vowel marks lost, so the options are indistinguishable
issues.detail: Card 1 asks the student to pick the right word from the brackets, but the options show as (فنجانَ - فنجان- فنجان): only the first keeps its vowel mark, the other two are identical bare words. The scheme answer is the bare word 'فنجان' as well, so it does not say which option is correct. The question cannot be answered or checked from the card.
issues.suggested_fix: Restore the diacritics (tanwin/case endings) from the paper for every option and the answer; if the text source cannot carry them, show a crop of the question line and of the scheme line instead.

issues.title: Underlined word not shown
issues.detail: Card 2 says to vowel the end of 'what is underlined' in the sentence, but the sentence 'صار القمح خبز.' has no underline on any word. The student has to guess which word is meant (the scheme shows it was 'خبز').
issues.suggested_fix: Underline the target word in the card text.

issues.title: Parsing scheme split at the wrong places
issues.detail: Card 4 (20 marks, parse the sentence) has four rows: the second runs two words' analyses together ('فاعل مرفوع بالضمة كتاب ابيك مضاف اليه ...لأنه من الأسماء') and the third row is the single leftover word 'الخمسة' with its own 4 marks, which is just the end of the previous phrase ('the five nouns'). The word each analysis belongs to is not set off.
issues.suggested_fix: One row per word parsed, word in bold followed by its analysis (أعجب / ني / كتاب / أبي / ك), with the marks the scheme gives each; or show the official scheme table as an image.

issues.title: Arabic in the scheme is small and left-aligned
issues.detail: Scheme answers are in about 13px text, left-aligned, while the question is roughly 20px and right-aligned. On the phone the answer word in cards 1 and 5 is the smallest thing in the box and harder to read than the English note under it.
issues.suggested_fix: Set scheme Arabic at the same size as question Arabic, dir=rtl and right-aligned.

issues.title: Boilerplate English note under every answer
issues.detail: Every first scheme row carries 'The paper is set in Arabic and the scheme answers in Arabic; this ask is answered in Arabic. Arabic reads right to left.' It is longer than the answer, says 'this ask', and tells an Arabic student nothing. On card 4 it appears under row one only, which looks random.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove it, or show it once as a small subject-level note outside the scheme rows.

issues.title: Footer strip scrambles mixed-direction text
issues.detail: The grey 'Not claimed yet · N marks · ...' strip joins English and several Arabic points in one line; on card 4 the points appear in reversed order with ellipses and 'and 1 more' in the middle of the Arabic.
issues.suggested_fix: Isolate each Arabic fragment (bdi / dir=auto) or drop the point text from the strip for RTL subjects.

issues.title: Passage run into the question as one block
issues.detail: Card 5 runs the instruction, the whole short passage, the 'extract from the text above' line and part (d) together as one paragraph, with no visual break between passage and task. Card 1 keeps a row of dots for the blank touching the next word.
issues.suggested_fix: Set the passage as an indented block, then the task on its own line; replace the dot leader with a short blank with spaces either side.

good_examples.why: Multiple-choice options each on their own line, correct passage attached, scheme names the option letter and its words.
Despite the run-on layout the text is fully legible with vowel marks kept, and the one-word answer is unambiguous.
